Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Idaho Falls District Office The Idaho Falls District, located in southeast Idaho, manages approximately 3.7 million acres of public land. The topography and terrain differ substantially throughout the area, ranging from sagebrush and desert to high-elevation forests. The District itself incorporates 16 counties, with Montana to the north and Utah to the south. The western edge borders the Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve, with the eastern edge extending to the beautiful Teton mountain range. With such a diverse geographic area, the Idaho Falls District has many challenges to face as it balances its mission of multiple use and sustainable yield to achieve a sustainable ecosystem. Some of the major activities occurring within the district include: grazing, recreation, mining, wildlife and fisheries, fire management, riparian and wetland management, realty and land use. The Idaho Falls District is divided into four geographic areas/field offices: Challis (799,000 acres), Salmon (493,000 acres), Upper Snake (1,854,000 acres) and Pocatello (557,000 acres). But for adults who never outgrew their fossil fascination, the Canadian province of Alberta offers a chance to explore the truth behind the fiction, witness new discoveries and touch real dinosaur bones with your bare hands. This journey back in time starts in southern Alberta, two hours east of Calgary, where the ground cracks open to reveal a prehistoric archive dating back some 76 million years. In this treeless desert, only the hardiest vegetation survives: yellow buffalo bean flowers and tiny pincushion cacti sprout between gullies, and the aroma of sagebrush hangs on the breeze. Existen distintos tipos de infecciones de oído. La infección del oído medio (otitis media aguda) es una infección en el oído medio. La otitis media exudativa es otra condición médica que afecta el oído medio. Esta ocurre cuando se acumula líquido en el oído medio sin causar una infección. No causa fiebre, dolor de oído ni acumulación de pus en el oído medio. El oído de nadador es una infección en el canal auditivo externo. Es distinto de una infección del oído medio. Close infraboiii's Diary Vending machines in France: what 7,800 OSM objects say about tagging Posted by infraboiii on 10 November 2026 in English . I maintain a map of vending machines built from OpenStreetMap data, part of a site that connects vending operators with venues (link at the end). It covers France, Belgium, Germany, Austria and Italy and is refreshed every month from Geofabrik extracts. While importing the 8 November 2026 extract, a few things about how vending machines are tagged stood out. I’m sharing them in case they are useful to mappers and data consumers. The numbers. The French extracts (mainland and overseas) contain 37,259 objects tagged amenity=vending_machine . The map shows 7,779 of them: those whose vending=* value (or, failing that, name ) is a product people seek out, such as food, drinks, bread, pizza, farm products, hygiene products and food lockers. Left out are, among others, machines with no identifiable product, cigarette machines and parcel lockers. The figures below refer to these 7,779 machines, compared with 17,924 selected the same way in Germany. Product mix. The most common values are condoms (1,456), pizza (1,425) and bread (934). Germany, with more than twice as many machines on the map, has 132 pizza and 42 bread machines. One machine, several products. In France, 1,530 machines (20%) list several products in a single semicolon-separated value, in no fixed order: drinks;sweets 418 times, sweets;drink

pages.text: Inside Paul Sereno's dinosaur hunt through the world’s fiercest desert | National Geographic By Paul Sereno Photographs by Keith Ladzinski Published July 15, 2025 As the Saharan sun rose on my waylaid team, one morning in September 2022, it seemed to burn with particular intensity. For nearly three weeks we’d been holed up in a mud-walled compound in the oasis town of Agadez, in central Niger, stalled because of officials’ insistence on assembling for us a large armed escort. Now, as dawn broke, we were finally ready to embark: Nearly a hundred people packed into 15 vehicles, a motley caravan of SUVs, pickups, and one large dump truck, all strapped with sand ladders and spare tires, heading out on an extraordinary desert dinosaur hunt—without question, the most ambitious of my career. ( "Lost" Fortresses of Sahara Revealed by Satellites) Among our number were Tuareg guides and drivers, a film crew, 64 armed guards, and my paleo dream team of 20 students and freshly minted professors, recruited to spend three months venturing across one of the planet’s least hospitable landscapes. Our mission was to explore and excavate three distinct sites, spread across hundreds of miles of blazing, roadless desert. pages.text: Inside the bone-crushing mating rituals of dinosaurs | National Geographic SCIENCE Inside the bone-crushing mating rituals of dinosaurs A handful of unique fossils are spilling the secrets of dinosaur courtship and reproduction. An Olorotitan dinosaur fossil with fractured tail vertebrae has resurrected a theory around how dinosaurs mated. Stocktrek Images, Alamy By Riley Black Published December 26, 2025 Whatever happened to the duck-billed dinosaur, it was a real pain in the butt. Many of the spines sitting atop the animal’s tail vertebrae had been fractured. The dinosaur, known as Olorotitan to paleontologists, wasn’t simply clumsy; too many bones were broken. The breaks were more consistent with some heavy downward pressure right near the base of the tail. At 26 feet long and three tons, another Olorotitan would have been large enough to do such damage. Institute of Natural Sciences in Brussels paleontologist Filippo Bertozzo had ventured to Blagoveshchensk, Russia’s Paleontologic Museum in 2019 to study the dinosaur’s bones when he noticed the strange injuries. “When I realized what I had in front of me, I had a cry of joy,” says Bertozzo. He had seen busted bones like these before in his research and in the scientific literature—fractured vertebrate near the hadrosaur’s hips. In 1989, paleontologist Darren Tanke suggested that similar breaks were the result of mating as one dinosaur mounted the other. pages.text: Inside the making of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi | National Geographic By Richard Conniff Photographs by Craig Cutler Published July 2, 2026 Dinosaurs are winging in at 550 miles an hour from across the planet: Diplodocus , Stegosaurus, a herd of Triceratops , and a pair of Tyrannosaurus rex (plus a carcass for the tyrannosaurs to do combat over). The museum has them in a queue, along with thousands of other specimens, from a fog-basking beetle to a reconstructed dodo. Some of them are awaiting takeoff, and some are in flight. Others are being uncrated, condition-checked, 3D-scanned, and quickly moved out for reassembly on the museum floor, all to make room for the next specimens just rolling through the delivery bay door. It’s early November 2025, and there are 20 days left until the opening of the Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi (NHMAD), a 377,000-square-foot structure being built and populated on what even the museum’s managers admit is an “insanely short” five-year timeline. With luck, the final major specimen—the last of five 75-foot-tall sauropods greeting visitors at the entrance—will arrive in time to go on display a day or two before the soft opening. That’s when Abu Dhabi’s royal families will arrive, fully expecting to be impressed. At the moment, however, that dinosaur, a Diplodocus, is still in Canada. And the mount is not yet complete. SBICs invest in small businesses in the form of debt and equity. The SBA doesn’t invest directly into small businesses, but it does provide funding to qualified SBICs with expertise in certain sectors or industries. Those SBICs then use their private funds, along with SBA-guaranteed funding, to invest in small businesses. What you can get SBICs invest in small businesses through debt, equity, or a combination of both. Debt is a loan an SBIC gives to a business, which the business must pay back, along with any interest. Equity is a share of ownership an SBIC gets in a business in exchange for providing funding. No, it's a 'miraculous' new prehistoric reptile Mirasaura grauvogeli had a featherlike crest and a tail like a monkey. “It's been a long time since I've been so blown away by a new fossil discovery.” By Asher Elbein Published July 23, 2025 Some 247 million years ago, a bizarre, six-inch-long reptile crept down a branch, its prehensile tail and feet clutching the bark like a monkey, and its narrow, birdlike face scanning its surroundings. On its back, an overlapping fan of stiff structures likely caught the light, vibrant with color. They looked very much like feathers, but were something entirely different as the reptile wasn’t related to birds or dinosaurs, and it existed a hundred million years before the first dinosaur took wing . Researchers have long believed things like feathers and fur—complex structures which grow out of the skin, and can be used for insulation, sensing surroundings, visual displays and allowing flight—are largely unique to the lineages that gave rise to birds and mammals. But now, a team of paleontologists have discovered a prehistoric reptile with a regal, plume-like crest that is unlike any previously-known integumentary appendage, things like horns, claws, and hair. Historian Sam Dalrymple travels to Greece to meet an archaeologist who made the discovery of a lifetime. In 343 B.C., Philip of Macedon invited Aristotle, the greatest philosopher of his age, to join his court as tutor to his son as head of the Mieza Gymnasium. Aristotle would not have known it then, but his pupil Alexander the Great would go on to remake the world. Artwork by Armet Portanell, Look and Learn/Bridgeman Images By Sam Dalrymple Published October 30, 2026 I’m Sam Dalrymple , a historian and author of Travels of Samwise and Shattered Lands: Five Partitions and the Making of Modern Asia . Today we're diving into the discovery of Aristotle’s gymnasium. And we'll be back next week covering a controversial dinosaur fossil auction. Sign up here to make sure you don't miss it! I set out to meet archaeologist Angeliki Kottaridi in mid-August, as the temperature of the Pierian range had begun to drop, and the first of the wild cyclamen was beginning to blossom across the Greek countryside. Kottaridi is an energetic eccentric, who began her career studying witches in Greek myth and is now the proud owner of several dozen cats. A former assistant to archaeologist Manolis Andronikos, who found Philip of Macedon's tomb in 1977, Kottaridi later led the Greek excavation of Failaka, the most important Hellenistic site in Kuwait. pages.description: James Botham is accustomed to working away from the spotlight, but his performance could not be denied against New Zealand.
pages.text: James Botham: Wales' unlikely hero in historic win over New Zealand - BBC Sport Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Image caption, James Botham was man of the match in Wales' historic win over New Zealand By Gareth Rhys Owen BBC Sport Wales Published 16 November 2026 James Botham lay sprawled on the Principality Stadium turf, pain and exhaustion etched across his face. Whenever the whistle blew, the Wales flanker in the red scrum cap took an age to rise. Precious seconds to recover. Nobody counts tackles when the ball is dead. But when play resumed, he was everywhere. Tackling, scrambling, hitting the deck and springing back up. By the final whistle, Botham had helped Wales beat New Zealand for the first time in 73 years. He was man of the match. And as the celebrations began, the tears flowed. Quite an afternoon for a player accustomed to working away from the spotlight. Keeping a Botham out of the headlines was always going to be difficult. His grandfather, Lord Ian Botham , is one of Britain's great sporting celebrities. Outspoken, charismatic and capable of turning cricket matches almost single-handedly, he is box-office. James is different. His game is built on tackles, chasing, wrestling and relentless graft. Few positions in rugby are less glamorous than blind-side flanker. But on Saturday, Wales' number six was the star of the show. Before arriving at the Department, Deputy Secretary Danly was a partner and the Energy Regulatory Group leader at Skadden in Washington, D.C. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us Considered an "Enemy Race" in Their Own Country This is how Western Defense Commander John L. DeWitt characterized people of Japanese ancestry during World War II. He insisted that even those who had been born and raised as U.S. citizens nevertheless posed a threat because their Japanese “racial strains” were “undiluted.” Under the authority of President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Executive Order 9066, DeWitt ordered the removal of all Japanese Americans from the West Coast in 1942. Allowed to take only what they could carry, they were imprisoned, without trial, in some of the most desolate places in the country. Today, the National Park Service preserves those sites so that visitors may learn their story. I spent two years mapping the areas surrounding one of the most beautiful drives in the world. Each morning, I looked forward to discovering and mapping an area adjacent to a one I did the day before. This diary entry serves as an introduction to a series of texts covering the challenges I encountered and how I overcame them. Included below are a few snapshots taken in the field, which capture the majestic landscapes along the Icefields Parkway. I have also added a “before and after” map excerpt, as well as a short video, to illustrate how my work gradually took shape over time. The Place The Icefields Parkway (Highway 93N), in Alberta, owes its name to the spectacular icefields and glaciers that line the road. The parkway, which is a 232 km stretch of highway cutting through Banff and Jasper National Parks, attracts between 1.2 million and 2 million visitors per year. The parkway offers exceptional alpine landscape, with glaciers, rivers, turquoise lakes, and breathtaking mountain views directly from the roadside (Figure 1). Jungle: Tiny Desk Concert November 2, 2026 5:00 AM ET Robin Hilton Credit: Photo: Lexy Beale/NPR It's hard for any band to make the old sound completely new, but Jungle has spent much of the past decade transforming vintage soul and R&B into something almost alien. The grooves are deep and warmly familiar, with wistful reflections on love and longing. But even in the brightest moments, there's often a thread of mystery and melancholy that leaves you questioning whether everything is as it seems. Fronted by the trio of Tom McFarland, Josh Lloyd-Watson and Lydia Kitto, Jungle is known for fluid live sets, with songs that spill into each other. True to form, at the Tiny Desk, they perform more than a half-dozen tracks that run together in a single, continuous groove. "We're gonna keep the music rolling," Lloyd-Watson tells the NPR crowd as the band melts seamlessly from 2018's "Beat 54 (All Good Now)" into "Dominoes" from the 2023 album Volcano. Sponsor Message The members are all smiles here, even as they sing about faded dreams ("Casio"), dead-end infatuations ("Someday, Somewhere") and the struggle to hold on when everything falls apart ("The Wave").
